10.1002_adfm.202518785: The bi‐layered hydrated vanadate is anticipated as a promising next‐generation cathode material for high‐energy zinc‐ion batteries. However, the practical application has been impeded by undesirable voltage fade, which originates from local structure distortion induced by zinc ion (de)intercalation. Herein, V 2 O 5 · n H 2 O pre‐intercalated with various organic cations is investigated to elucidate the relationship between electronic structure modulation and voltage variations during local structure evolution. Microscopic scale observations—using ex situ X‐ray diffraction, synchrotron X‐ray pair distribution function along with X‐ray absorption fine structure spectroscopy—reveal that the electronic structure perturbation is governed by the distortion of [VO 6 ] octahedra, which leads to V 3 d orbitals splitting. Specifically, the structural distortion induces variations in vanadium‐oxygen bond lengths and alters the ligand‐field electronic structure, boosting the operating voltage (44 mV higher midpoint voltage) and cycling stability (91.3% retention after 3000 cycles). These findings reveal a fundamental correlation for the development of high‐energy‐density batteries with superior stability through local structural design.
10.1002_adfm.74739: Protonic Ceramic Fuel Cells In their Research Article (10.1002/adfm.202525258), Ho-Il Ji, Sihyuk Choi, and co-workers present a rationally designed cathode microstructure for protonic ceramic fuel cells, featuring a thermomechanically compatible backbone decorated with electrochemically active nanocatalysts. This synergistic cathode design effectively mitigates thermal expansion mismatch while expanding electrochemically active sites, thereby delivering high power output and outstanding thermal cycling stability in fuel cell operation.
10.1002_aenm.71166: Industrial water electrolysis (WE) requires oxygen evolution electrodes that combine intrinsic catalytic activity with efficient mass transport under high current densities. Here, we report a single‐step femtosecond‐laser interfacial engineering strategy to fabricate self‐supporting nickel‐based anodes with hierarchical micro/nano architectures and oxygen‐vacancy‐related surface features. This interfacial design simultaneously provides superhydrophilic/superaerophobic wettability for rapid gas‐liquid transport and modulates surface electronic properties for enhanced oxygen evolution reaction (OER) activity. As a result, the laser‐structured electrode exhibits enhanced OER activity together with robust operational stability under industrially relevant conditions. When integrated into an anion exchange membrane water electrolyzer (AEMWE), the system achieves a voltage of 1.81 V at 1000 mA cm −2 alongside exceptional durability over 1000 h with a negligible voltage decay rate. This scalable laser‐enabled strategy provides a versatile platform for designing efficient and stable electrode for sustainable hydrogen production.
10.1039_d5ee06874f: We developed an azo-linked conjugated polymer anode via an in situ electrochemical synthesis strategy, which provides a sustainable and cost-effective alternative for large-scale energy storage by avoiding toxic heavy metals or expensive alloys.
